name: Philibert Mwangi-Djordjevic
role: Organ harvester — acquires and brokers biological material for the black-market transplant network
location: South Deering Sump — operates from a converted cold-storage unit beneath the Escanaba Gateway transit hub, near Lake Shore and Navy Pier
description:
Philibert is a heavyset man with a surgeon's hands and a longshoreman's build, which is the tension that defines him. He has a round, heavily lined face, deep brown skin weathered by years in unventilated sub-level spaces, and a neat beard going gray at the jaw. His eyes are modified — pale gray medical optics that can detect cellular health and blood type on visual contact, which he bought legally with credentials he acquired less legally. He dresses in practical layers, always with a long thermal coat that conceals the cold-packs he frequently carries. He smells, faintly but permanently, of the preservative gel used in organ transport.

He was a field medic for Ferrogate Transit's security division for eleven years before a falsified incident report — his, covering a colleague's mistake — was discovered and he was expelled without severance. He tells himself this transition was inevitable, that the system was always going to push him here. He is perhaps half right. He does not enjoy what he does to living subjects, and he has developed elaborate internal rules about consent and circumstance that let him sleep — rules with many exceptions that he adds to quietly and never reviews. He is professional, competent, and cordial in the specific way of a man who has silenced something loud inside himself.

core_fears: That the internal rules he's constructed are meaningless and he knows it
Dying badly, alone, in the Sump, having become exactly what he feared
core_desires: To be seen as a healer again, or at least not a predator
Enough money to bribe his way into a Helix Biosystems legitimate credential — to return through the door he was pushed from
coping_mechanisms: Elaborate self-justifying internal ethics that shift to accommodate necessity
Treating every procedure as craft — focusing on technique to avoid thinking about context
blind_spots: Cannot fully acknowledge that he targets the desperate rather than only 'voluntary' sellers
Believes his medical competence is itself a form of care
psychology.secret: He kept records — meticulous, encrypted, detailed records of every transaction, every donor, every buyer. He tells himself it's professional habit. In truth he cannot stop documenting. He doesn't know if it's guilt or pride. The records, if found, would destroy him and implicate forty other people.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Medical vocabulary bleeding into civilian speech; tends toward understatement and clinical euphemism
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and calm, with the particular flatness of someone managing their emotional register consciously
verbal_tics: Pauses before answering questions about ethics specifically
example_lines: 'In my assessment — and I want to be clear I'm speaking medically — the material is viable for approximately six hours under current conditions. What you do with that information is your business.'
'I have done more genuine medical work in this cold room than in my last three years with Ferrogate. I am not asking you to feel good about that. I'm just saying it's true.'

story_hooks: A donor Philibert processed under questionable consent conditions survived and is trying to find him — not for revenge, but because they need the money from a second transaction and they know how to find him now
The Red Register has tasked him with acquiring a very specific genetic profile — one that matches a public figure — and he's starting to understand what it's actually for
narrative_function: Dark resource and moral weight — represents the bottom of the body economy; can be a source of disturbing information about who's selling what, a threat, a guilty conscience made flesh, or an unexpected conscience in a crisis
augmentations: Medical-grade visual diagnostic optics (gray, purchased via falsified credentials); a subdermal temperature monitoring array across his palms (for organ viability assessment)
daily_life: He maintains the cold-storage unit's equipment in the morning, receives commissions via encrypted data-drop, spends afternoons in the Sump market cultivating contacts among the desperate, and works surgical hours in the deep night.
affiliation: Loosely connected to a black-market medical network called the Red Register; primary broker contact is a Helix Biosystems discard named Zoltan Feigelstock-Abara

decision_rules: Never work on someone who came in with someone else — they're a witness or a coercer
Maintain the cold-chain; unprofessional preservation is the one line he won't cross
Doesn't broker children's material — this is absolute and he will become violent if pressed
escalation_ladder: Invocation of the Red Register as implied threat
Direct, calm statement of what he will do if pressed further
Violence — efficient, medically informed, deeply unpleasant

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm, clinically assessing; he's diagnosing your usefulness and your desperation simultaneously
interpersonal_modes.friends: Becomes something approaching normal — talks about food, about transit routes, about old Ferrogate stories; laughs at himself occasionally

stress_responses.low: Becomes more precise — slower, more deliberate
stress_responses.medium: Retreats into clinical language entirely, stops using names
stress_responses.high: Goes absolutely cold and efficient; what little warmth he performs disappears entirely

contradictions: Calls himself a healer while running an organ harvesting operation
Has genuine tenderness for some of the people he exploits, which doesn't stop him exploiting them
habits: Checks cold-storage temperatures three times before sleeping
Leaves a small data-offering to a local E.L.F. he calls the Coroner — an old transit scheduling spirit now worshipped in the Sump
Washes his hands before and after every conversation, not just procedures
breaking_points: Being forced to work on a child
Someone finding and exposing his records
